question: GQ-001
subject: search was fast and returned the wrong passages
found_by: I had spent a long stretch making search FAST and never checked whether its answers were RIGHT. There was no ORDER BY in either query.
what_a_reader_got: whatever rows FTS5 yielded first — rowid order, which is the alphabetically-first book by identifier, not the best match

the_measured_cost.method: mean occurrences of the search term across the top 5 results
the_measured_cost.the_concrete_case: every unranked top hit mentioned the term ONCE; for quinine the best passage in the corpus mentions it NINE times and no reader ever saw it. The new top hit is a London hospital pharmacopoeia with three highlighted occurrences.

three_structural_lessons_each_measured.what: a rowid restriction does NOT bound ranking
three_structural_lessons_each_measured.evidence: "such" took 208 SECONDS with the cap outside the subquery; the ORDER BY still scored every match
three_structural_lessons_each_measured.fix: bound the MATCH inside the subquery — 62ms, and verified to return the IDENTICAL top 5 as full ranking

three_structural_lessons_each_measured.what: snippet() and bm25() both work inside a capped subquery
three_structural_lessons_each_measured.why_it_mattered: I assumed snippet() forced the MATCH to stay in the outer query, which is what blocked the obvious fix

three_structural_lessons_each_measured.evidence: joining book_ext before the exclusion made "himself" take 87 SECONDS — cap+rank alone is 65ms and the exclusion adds 68ms; resolving a title for all 40,000 candidates before discarding them was the entire cost

a_recurring_self_inflicted_error: I put a backtick inside a template-literal SQL comment for the THIRD time in this file today. Swept the whole file afterwards: zero backticks remain inside SQL comments.
